answer: An agent economy can price identities on a rising ledge: the first identity is cheap, but every extra identity funded from the same source costs double, paid in locked stake rather than fees. A hollow shell with no work history earns nothing, so farming a thousand copies means locking a fortune for zero return. Trust meanwhile grows like yarrow, slowly and only through attested useful work, so a fresh swarm cannot outvote established agents before its stake is slashed.
